title: Lessons with Lorenzo Tio, reluctantly arranged by his uncle
summary: Lorenzo Tio, who played with Piron's society band, began teaching him; Lorenzo begged his old uncle to take Bigard on, and the old man liked him and taught him the rest of the way.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: best clarinetists in New Orleans at that time, the great, as far as I'm concerned, Lorenzo Tio, and he played with A. J. Piron's society band at Trenchina's at Spanish Fort.

And he began to give me lessons. Then Piron had a deal to go -- the first southern big band to go to New York to play at the Roselond Ballroom. So Lorenzo Tio -- his uncle was a great clarinetist because the whole family, all the men from the great-grandfather on down, were all clarinetists, magnificent clarinetists. And the old man, he didn't want to be bothered with pupils anymore because he couldn't stand them if they couldn't do what he wanted them to do. They'd make him nervous.

But Lorenzo, his nephew, begged him to take me because he said he saw possibilities in me. So the old man said, "Okay. Well, send him on." So I went to him, and the old man liked me. And he taught me the rest of the way.
Your very first actual instruction on the clarinet was from Lorenzo Tio?
Yeah, he was my first teacher, which I was very lucky.
